title: Practise the formats before they count
statement: Let learners practise the formats and interactions of the test that counts before it counts, because meeting an unfamiliar interface on the scored test adds noise to the score.
example: One reading course runs a 43-item practice lane for format exposure that never feeds a mastery gate.
detail: A reading assessment's position is that learners who practised only single-select items met multi-select and two-part evidence items for the first time on the scored official test, and that interface novelty is construct-irrelevant variance, citing the testing standards (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/00_BRAINLIFT.md`). A Grade 8 reading course runs a 43-item practice lane in three formats for format exposure, never routed through a mastery gate (`incept-package-hub/course-packages/courses/g8-reading/review/evidence/case-for-review.md`).
against: The package's own audit later bounded the benefit: strongest for the three formats confirmed for the official reading test, low-harm extra practice for the other three (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/00_AUDITS_AND_FIXES.md`). An adversarial review added that if familiarity moves scores at all, it moves the official ones, which matters when the practice doubles as a validation study (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/red-team/RED_TEAM_FINDINGS.md`). Format practice can inflate an internal growth reading, so one course measures growth on a held-out instrument it never teaches to or gates on (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5_build_2026_07_02/approval_clean.md`).

evidence.quote: Alpha students practice on 100% MCQ material; their first multi-select or two-part evidence item is on the scored official MAP. Interface novelty is construct-irrelevant variance (AERA/APA/NCME Standard 1.13).
